passages.original: Deinde quod de Con- stantini lepra ejusque baptismo in Silvestri papae f(??)lsis gestis ac pseudoconstituto fingitur, repetit., Quod autem Ensebius Caesariensis episcopus de Con- stantini Magni baptismo Nicomediae ab Eusebio civi- tatia hujus praesule suscepto tradit, de fictilii hujus nepotis baptismo stolide Interpretatur. Neque minus fals(??) haeroticam de pluribus Mariae filiis opinionem Constantio attribuit. Quis vero cum turpiter halluci- nari non sentiat, ubi exilli Liberii vel causam vel lo- cum exponit?
passages.english: Next, he repeats what is invented about Constantine's leprosy and his baptism in the false Acts of Pope Silvester and the pseudo-constitution. And what Eusebius, bishop of Caesarea, relates about the baptism of Constantine the Great, received at Nicomedia from Eusebius, the prelate of that city, he stupidly interprets as concerning the baptism of this fictitious nephew. No less falsely does he attribute to Constantius the heretical opinion about several sons of Mary. And who would not perceive that he blunders shamefully where he sets out either the cause or the place of Liberius' exile?
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'f(??)lsis' read as 'falsis', 'Ensebius' as 'Eusebius', 'civitatia' as 'civitatis', 'fals(??)' as 'falso', 'haeroticam' as 'haereticam', 'exilli' as 'exilii'. 'fictilii' is taken as 'fictitii' (fictitious). 'Pseudo-constitution' is the forged Constitutum attributed to Silvester.

passages.original: quod Constantii imperatoris cum Liberio dialogus, hactenus Athanasium ab ipso damnatum non esse fidem facit; quod denique ipse Liberius a defendendi Athanasii studio jam dejectus, se hac tenus in illo defendendo constantem fuisse osten– dit, cum constantiae hujus hanc reddit rationem : « Quia susceperat illum bonae memoriae Julius epi- scopus decessor meus; verebar ne ab aliquo prae- varicator judicarer. » Hujusmodi argumenta fusius exposita, et alia nonnulla, quae sequentis epistolae falsitatem demonstrant, apud Hilarium fragro, iv vi- dere licet. Et vero Hilarius in annotationibus, quasi epistolae huic subjecit, de illa sic loquitur, ut qui eam a Potamio et Epitecto conficiam, ac deinde a Fortu- natiano Aquileiensi episcopo ad diversos episcopos missam esse existimarit.
passages.english: that the dialogue of the emperor Constantius with Liberius gives proof that Athanasius had not yet been condemned by him; and finally that Liberius himself, though already turned away from his zeal for defending Athanasius, shows that up to then he had been steadfast in defending him, since he gives this reason for that steadfastness: "Because Julius of good memory, the bishop who preceded me, had received him; I was afraid that I might be judged a transgressor by someone." Arguments of this kind, set out more fully, and some others which demonstrate the falsity of the following letter, can be seen in Hilary, fragment IV. And indeed Hilary, in the annotations which he attached, as it were, to this letter, speaks of it in such a way as one who judged that it was composed by Potamius and Epictetus, and then sent by Fortunatianus, bishop of Aquileia, to various bishops.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence, continuing a list of arguments from the preceding context. 'fragro, iv' is read as 'fragm. IV'. 'Epitecto' is taken as Epictetus, and 'conficiam' as 'confectam' (composed). The opening 'quod ... dialogus' clause seems to lack a verb or to be garbled; it is translated by sense.
